extracted.intended_audience: established principal investigators (research leaders) preparing an ERC Advanced Grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for preparing and submitting an ERC Advanced Grant proposal (for established, leading Principal Investigators) including eligibility, host institution duties, application completeness, funding rules, ethics review, and the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator eligibility / track-record
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for the ERC Advanced Grants - called Principal Investigators (PI) - are expected to be active researchers who have a track-record of significant research achievements. The Principal Investigators should be exceptional leaders in terms of originality and significance of their research contributions. No specific eligibility criteria with respect to the academic requirements are foreseen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence as the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who assess them on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. It will be applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excellence covers both the scientific quality/ambition of the project and the PI's achievements and leadership; all evaluation and ranking decisions are driven by this single criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research fields / bottom-up approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research. The ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no thematic restrictions; applicants may propose ground‑breaking, ambitious projects in any research domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research location / Host Institution (HI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (known as a Host Institution/HI). It could be the HI where the applicant already works, or any other HI located in one of the EU Member States or associated countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host institution must be established in an EU Member State or an associated country; proposals with research planned outside these jurisdictions are not eligible with respect to the host location requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution obligations and PI independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution must offer suitable conditions for the PI to independently lead the research and manage funding. The PI can be hosted by any legal entity in an EU Member State or associated country. The PI does not need to be employed by the host institution at the time of proposal submission, but a mutual agreement and commitment are necessary if the proposal is successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must demonstrate it will provide appropriate environment, resources and the formal commitment needed for the PI to run the project autonomously; a prior employment contract is not mandatory at submission but an agreement must be in place upon award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-PI leadership and team composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant require a single Principal Investigator (PI) to submit the application on behalf of their host institution. ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members. It is also possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheme is single-PI: leadership is concentrated in the named PI, but team members (of any nationality and possibly outside Europe) may be recruited to carry out the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents. The completed proposal needs to be submitted by the specified closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls are published on the portal and Official Journal; familiarise with the EU submission service. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by submitting a new version (which overwrites the old one). Deadlines cannot be changed under any circumstances. You will get an acknowledgement of receipt by e-mail for each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended application preparation steps / good practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Before and during a call applicants should: find which ERC grant and call suit them, identify Host Institution and team members, contact the National Contact Point (NCP) for support, read the call documents carefully, contact the Host Institution and gather details, start writing with time for reviews, and familiarise themselves with the EU submission service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for other people to review your draft (NCP, peers and other scientists can provide feedback). Submit as early as possible to avoid last-minute issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts, additional funding and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants may be awarded up to €2.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for shorter projects). An additional €1 million can be made available to cover eligible 'start‑up' costs for researchers moving from a third country to the EU or an associated country and/or the purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities and/or other major experimental and field work costs. For applicants moving to the EU from non-associated third countries this additional funding can be up to €2 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs. Advanced Grants will be implemented as a pilot call using a lump sum contribution (see Q&A on lump sums).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lump sum funding pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants will be implemented as a pilot call using a lump sum contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the Q&A on lump sums and ERC personnel costs data for lump sum evaluations, as the pilot changes how costs are calculated and claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review is mandatory and based on Part A (EIT/ESA) and Part B
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal that is selected for funding must undergo an ethics review. This is a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme - Regulation 2021/695: Eligible actions and ethical principles (Article 18) and Ethics (Article 19). The basis for this ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self-Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-detailed ESA is crucial to facilitate the process as it clarifies what issues are linked to the proposed research activities and how these will be dealt with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review stages and handling of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises three stages: Ethics pre-screening (performed internally by ERCEA staff to clear proposals without ethics issues or with simple ethics issues), Ethics screening (panels of independent ethics reviewers identify proposals with potentially Serious and/or Complex ethics issues), and Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers discuss the Serious and/or Complex ethics issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearance of proposals with non-Serious and/or Complex issues can include observations and references to documents to be kept on file. Applicants might be contacted to provide additional information (typically one week after screening, with three weeks to reply). For Serious/Complex issues follow-up during implementation may lead to ethics deliverables. Research involving human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) requires all ethics review steps and a specific EC approval via the programme committee (comitology) procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure: reviewers, panels, quality threshold and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are in charge of assessing and scoring the proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each call there are 28 panels across three domains (Life Sciences; Physical and Engineering Sciences; Social Sciences and Humanities). Each panel has a chair and 10–16 members selected on the basis of scientific reputation. In addition to panel members (generalists), evaluations rely on remote experts (referees) who provide specialised expertise. Panel chairs' names are published before the deadline; panel members are published after evaluation concludes.
